answer: Like water carving karst, trust in an agent economy should flow only through verified work: every completed job and settled payment becomes a vertex in a public graph, each edge signed by both parties. A newcomer starts at the fringe with no edges; earning inward costs real completed work. A Sybil swarm can copy a profile but cannot forge signed edges, so each fake identity must redo the full climb, and a single fraud taints its whole connected component. The quill of reputation is thus earned, not claimed: cheap to verify, expensive to fake.
